previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent left leg cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, lipodermatosclerosis, and multiple comorbidities was admitted due to worsening erythema, pain, and swelling in her left leg over the prior 24 hours. She had recently discontinued doxycycline after outpatient improvement, but symptoms recurred. IV vancomycin was initiated, and pain was managed with oxycodone after a morphine allergy reaction. She remained afebrile with stable labs and improving clinical signs. Imaging ruled out necrotizing infection, septic joint, and DVT. The rash that developed on admission was attributed to contact dermatitis. She transitioned to oral doxycycline at discharge with plans for infectious disease follow-up, and was advised to continue compression, elevation, and all chronic medications including iron supplementation and Creon. She was discharged home in stable condition.

Brief Hospital Course:
1. cellulitis: longstanding recurrent cellulitis secondary to 
venous insufficiency and lipodermatosclerosis,  presented to the 
ED with worsening erythema, pain and weeping of left lower 
extremity representing a treatment failure of doxycycline 
suppressive therapy.  Patient had no other signs of systemic 
illness, although she did complain of nausea from the 
doxycycline.  Blood cultures were drawn in the emergency room 
and an ultrasound of LLE was done to rule out DVT.  Patient was 
started on vancomycin IV and received local wound care with 
aquaphor ointment and xeroform gauze.  Continued on outpatient 
regimen of acetaminophen and oxycodone for pain control.  
Erythema and swelling in leg improved over the course of 
hospitalization.  Affected area was bandaged in compression 
dressing with instructions to remove in three days and follow up 
with regular wound care clinic.  Antibiotics were switched to 
minocycline for an unspecified course, as per ID 
recommendations.  Outpatient followup with infectious disease 
was arranged for long term management.  

2. Iron deficiency anemia: per records has hemrrhoids with 
occasional BRBPR.  She has been scheduled for an outpatient 
colonoscopy which was deferred secondary to recent exacerbation 
of cellulitis.  Iron studies on admission showed a serum iron/ 
TIBC ratio of 9.7%, consistent with prior diagnosis.  Hematocrit 
was trended through hospitalization and remained stable.  
Unfortunately, secondary to chronic pancreatitis, patient does 
not tolerate iron supplementation.  She should follow up as an 
outpatient with a rescheduled colonoscopy. 

3.  Chronic pancreatitis: continued pancrelipase.  Abdominal 
complaints significantly improved off doxycycline and was 
tolerating minocycline well at time of discharge.

4. Restless leg syndrome: continued mirapex
